changedBeliefs: Exp 234's per-occurrence blob-param wrapping carried a latent aliasing regression: `wrapBlobParams` called `TransferableTypedData.fromList` once per qualifying position, so a caller passing the SAME `Uint8List` object to N positions (or reusing one buffer across a coalesced `MultiExecuteRequest` burst) got N independent external copies of one buffer. That is strictly worse than the graph copy exp 234 replaced, because `SendPort.send`'s object-graph copy preserves reference identity and would have copied the shared buffer once. The regression is invisible on single-reference writes (the common case) and only bites when one buffer is referenced multiple times in a send.

The fix is the 'table protocol': wrap by identity via an identity-keyed cache (`HashMap(equals: identical, hashCode: identityHashCode)`), sharing ONE `TransferableTypedData` per unique backing buffer referenced at every occurrence. The graph copier sends the shared wrapper once (identity preserved across the hop); the writer materializes each unique wrapper exactly once (a second `materialize()` throws), so `unwrapBlobParams` dedups by wrapper identity and `_handleMultiExecute` threads one shared unwrap cache across the envelope's writes. Distinct buffers are unchanged (each still gets its own wrapper); the no-large-blob fast path still returns the input list with no allocation.

Isolated transport (one 300 KB buffer referenced N times, `alias_transfer_isolated.dart`) ranks three wrapping shapes and the table protocol dominates at every N: table 32.9/27.0/28.2/33.8/56.5 us at N=1/2/4/8/32 (flat); baseline (N TTD) 44.4/49.6/70.8/132.0/1502.7 us (linear blowup — the regression, ~27x table at N=32); census (leave aliased on the graph copy) ~180-210 us flat (one copy, but the large HEAP blob aborts onto the chunked `CopyTypedDataBaseWithSafepointChecks` slow path AND re-lands on the GC heap — the exact cost exp 234 exists to avoid). Table = baseline's single fast external copy + census's shared-once transport, with neither downside, and peak external memory drops from N buffers to 1. Table even edges baseline at N=1 (same single wrap; the gap is noise).
nextSignals: The write-side blob transfer story is now complete for aliasing: single reference (exp 234), coalesced envelopes (exp 234 review pass), and multi-reference/aliased buffers (exp 243). No open aliasing sub-case remains on the write path.

Census (leave aliased buffers on the graph-copy path) would only become competitive if a future Dart VM change gave large heap typed-data a fast unchunked graph-copy path — then 'leave it on the graph copy' would stop paying the slow-path tax and could rival table without wrapper bookkeeping. Nothing in current SDK behavior points that way; revisit only if `object_graph_copy.cc`'s large-typed-data handling changes.

The table protocol is a write-envelope concern and does NOT transfer to reads: a read response's blob cells are distinct materialized objects with no caller aliasing to collapse (exp 236 handles read-cell transfer). Do not add an identity-dedup layer to the read path looking for a symmetric win — the shape that makes table pay off (one caller object referenced N times) does not exist there.

claims.text: Blob-param wrapping is identity-keyed (one wrapper per unique buffer, referenced at every position, materialized once per envelope), so caller aliasing survives the hop instead of exploding into N external copies (~27x at N=32 under per-occurrence wrapping).
